text:
Emily: Hey team — noticed client process memory/FD count creeping after a load test. After ~10k concurrent requests our Python async SDK instance is at 600+ open fds and we see `Semaphore limit exceeded` in logs. Anyone else seen this with the new retry/auth patch?
Ben: ugh, I saw a hint of that yesterday in staging but chalked it up to test harness. Can you paste the minimal repro?
Emily: repro is small: high-concurrency aiohttp workers hitting the same shared RedwoodClient instance. We use a global `ClientSession` + our wrapper. Error looks like: `RuntimeError: semaphore at 0 cannot acquire` and a cascade of `Transport is closing` errors.
Jin: can you share logs and the client init? Might be connection pooling + our new backoff interacting badly.
Emily: logs: ``
2026-03-15T14:32:10Z ERROR worker-14 semaphore at 0 cannot acquire
2026-03-15T14:32:10Z WARN worker-14 failed request retry, leaving session open
2026-03-15T14:32:12Z ERROR worker-14 OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files
``
Emily: client snippet: ``
class AppClient:
    def __init__(self, api_key):
        self._session = ClientSession()
        self._client = RedwoodAsyncClient(api_key=api_key, session=self._session)

    async def request(self, payload):
        return await self._client.generate(payload)
``
Sana: two quick things to check: 1) are you using a single shared `RedwoodAsyncClient` across tasks? 2) did you upgrade to the retry change last week (it can spawn short-lived sessions on failures)?
Emily: yes to both. We were trying to share the client but I see some code paths calling `RedwoodAsyncClient(...)` again on auth refresh.
Ben: that rings a bell — the auth-refresh path in #2345 lazily creates a temporary client for the refresh and doesn't `close()` it on error. If many of those spawn under bursty auth failures, you'll leak transports.
Jin: repro idea: simulate auth token expiry + 100 concurrent requests, check FD churn. We should also check semaphore logic in our request throttler — if many tasks get cancelled, semaphores may not be released if exceptions aren't handled.
Emily: adding a try/finally to ensure `semaphore.release()` helped in local test. Also explicitly closing the temp client fixed FD leak.
Sana: good find. Two follow-ups: 1) SDK should avoid creating unclosed ephemeral clients in auth logic, 2) ensure we always `async with` or call `await client.close()` in error paths. Might add a finalizer to the client to log if not closed.
Ben: agree. I'll open a patch: remove ephemeral client allocation by using the existing session + token refresh hook. If we must create one, ensure it's used in an `async with` context or closed in finally.
Jin: small defensive change: wrap semaphore acquisition in `try:
    await sem.acquire()
except Exception:
    # log and re-raise
    raise
finally:
    if acquired:
        sem.release()` — but be careful with ordering on cancellations. Use `asyncio.shield` around critical sections when needed.
Emily: thanks. Quick mitigation for ops: reduce `max_concurrency` in workers and bump ulimit for fd on the pod. Also restart service after deploy.
ops-bot: Deploy queued: hotfix/semaphore-fix -> staging. CI job 4821 started. :rocket:
Ben: PR opened: github.com/redwood/py-sdk/pull/2412 — it removes ephemeral client creation in auth and adds a test that asserts no FD leak under 2000 concurrent auth refreshes.
Sana: nice. Add a typing/typing note — make the client `asynccontextmanager` so linters will warn on unclosed usage. Also add a runtime warning in `__del__` if not closed, but keep it opt-in for users who rely on GC behavior.
Emily: will validate tomorrow with the bigger load. Thanks all! :pray:
